mission_08: Robust statistics provides methods that are resistant to the influence of outliers, producing reliable estimates even when a portion of the data is corrupted. In regression, Ordinary Least Squares (OLS) minimizes squared residuals, making it highly sensitive to outliers that can dramatically skew the fitted line. Huber Regression uses the Huber loss function, which is quadratic for small residuals (like OLS) but linear for large residuals, reducing the influence of outliers. RANSAC (Random Sample Consensus) takes a different approach by repeatedly fitting models to random subsets of data and selecting the model with the most inliers. These robust methods are essential when outliers cannot be reliably removed or when the cost of manual outlier inspection is prohibitive. They provide a principled alternative to the detect-and-remove paradigm.
